claim: Deep learning models are efficiently used in laboratories for behavior analysis.
source: Deep learning models are efficiently used in laboratories for behavior analysis.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract about the current state of the field.

claim: It has not been achieved to use an end-to-end unsupervised neural network to extract comprehensive and discriminative features directly from social behavior video frames for annotation and analysis purposes.
source: However, it has not been achieved to use an end-to-end unsupervised neural network to extract comprehensive and discriminative features directly from social behavior video frames for annotation and analysis purposes.
evidence: This statement claims a gap in the existing literature that the current work addresses.

claim: Selfee is a self-supervised feature extraction convolutional neural network with multiple downstream applications to process video frames of animal behavior in an end-to-end way.
source: Here, we report a self-supervised feature extraction (Selfee) convolutional neural network with multiple downstream applications to process video frames of animal behavior in an end-to-end way.
evidence: This is the main contribution described in the abstract.

claim: Visualization and classification of the extracted features (Meta-representations) validate that Selfee processes animal behaviors in a way similar to human perception.
source: Visualization and classification of the extracted features (Meta-representations) validate that Selfee processes animal behaviors in a way similar to human perception.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Meta-representations can be efficiently used to detect anomalous behaviors that are indiscernible to human observation.
source: We demonstrate that Meta-representations can be efficiently used to detect anomalous behaviors that are indiscernible to human observation and hint in-depth analysis.
evidence: This is demonstrated through anomaly detection experiments in the manuscript.

claim: Time-series analyses of Meta-representations reveal the temporal dynamics of animal behaviors.
source: Furthermore, time-series analyses of Meta-representations reveal the temporal dynamics of animal behaviors.
evidence: This is supported by AR-HMM and DTW analyses presented in the results.

claim: Human observations and descriptions are the primary solutions for animal behavior analysis.
source: Traditionally, human observations and descriptions are the primary solutions for animal behavior analysis (Hall, 1994; McGill, 1962; Rubenstein and Alcock, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Supervised learning has been assisting human annotations and achieved impressive results.
source: With the emergence and flourish of machine learning methodology, supervised learning has been assisting human annotations and achieved impressive results (Jiang et al., 2019; Kabra et al., 2013; Segalin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Supervised learning is limited by prior knowledge and manually assigned labels, thus could not identify behavioral features that are not annotated.
source: Nevertheless, supervised learning is limited by prior knowledge (especially used for feature engineering) and manually assigned labels, thus could not identify behavioral features that are not annotated.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of supervised learning.

claim: Key points generated by pose estimation are less effective for direct behavior classification or two-dimensional visualization.
source: However, it has been demonstrated that the key points generated by pose estimation are less effective for direct behavior classification or two-dimensional visualization (Luxem et al., 2020; Sun et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The position of the proboscis of a fly is commonly neglected in behavior studies using pose estimation software.
source: Additionally, the neglection of body parts could cause problems. For example, the position of the proboscis of a fly is commonly neglected in behavior studies using pose estimation software (Calhoun et al., 2019; Sun et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The position of the proboscis is crucial for feeding, licking behavior during courtship, and hardness detection for a substrate.
source: Still, it is crucial for feeding (Zhou et al., 2019), licking behavior during courtship (Mezzera et al., 2020), and hardness detection for a substrate (Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There is no demonstration of pose-estimation methods applied to multiple animals of the same color with intensive interactions.
source: Finally, best to our knowledge, there is no demonstration of these pose-estimation methods applied to multiple animals of the same color with intensive interactions.
evidence: This is a claim about the state of the literature based on the authors' knowledge.

claim: Labeling body parts during mice mounting is challenging even for humans.
source: Thus, the application of pose estimation to mating behaviors of two black mice, a broadly adopted behavior paradigm (Bayless et al., 2019; Wei et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2021), could be limited because labeling body parts during mice mounting is challenging even for humans (see Discussion for more details).
evidence: This is supported by citations and refers to further discussion in the manuscript.

claim: CNNs have been proven more potent than classic computer vision algorithms like wavelet transforms and Radon transforms on the MNIST dataset, even without supervising.
source: Flourished deep learning methods, especially convolutional neural networks (CNNs) (Lecun et al., 1998), could adaptively extract features from diversified datasets. Also, they have been proven more potent than classic computer vision algorithms like wavelet transforms (Romero et al., 2009) and Radon transforms (Aradhya et al., 2007) on a famous grayscale dataset MNIST, even without supervising (Ji et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Cutting-edge self-supervised deep learning methods aim to extract representative features for downstream missions by comparing different augmentations of the same image and/or different images.
source: The cutting-edge self-supervised deep learning methods aim to extract representative features for downstream missions by comparing different augmentations of the same image and/or different images (Caron et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2020; Grill et al., 2020; He et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent self-supervised learning literature.

claim: Self-supervised or unsupervised methods could completely avoid human biases.
source: First, self-supervised or unsupervised methods could completely avoid human biases.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the advantages of self-supervised methods.

claim: The augmentations used to create positive samples promise invariance of the neural networks to object sizes, spatial orientations, and ambient laminations so that registration or other preprocessing is not required.
source: Second, the augmentations used to create positive samples promise invariance of the neural networks to object sizes, spatial orientations, and ambient laminations so that registration or other preprocessing is not required.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the properties of self-supervised learning with augmentations.

claim: The networks are optimized to export similar results for positive samples and separate negative ones, such that the extracted features are inherently discriminative.
source: Finally, the networks are optimized to export similar results for positive samples and separate negative ones, such that the extracted features are inherently discriminative.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the training objective of self-supervised learning.

claim: Networks can utilize differential information within batches to obtain remarkable results on downstream missions like classification or image segmentation even without negative samples.
source: Even without negative samples, the networks can utilize differential information within batches to obtain remarkable results on downstream missions like classification or image segmentation (Chen and He, 2021; Grill et al., 2020; Zbontar et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Selfee is trained on massive unlabeled behavior video frames (around five million frames from hundreds of videos) to avoid human bias in annotating animal behaviors.
source: Selfee is trained on massive unlabeled behavior video frames (around five million frames from hundreds of videos) to avoid human bias in annotating animal behaviors, and it could capture a global character of animal behaviors even when detailed postures are hard to extract, similar to human perception.
evidence: This describes the training data used for Selfee.

claim: Selfee could capture a global character of animal behaviors even when detailed postures are hard to extract, similar to human perception.
source: Selfee is trained on massive unlabeled behavior video frames (around five million frames from hundreds of videos) to avoid human bias in annotating animal behaviors, and it could capture a global character of animal behaviors even when detailed postures are hard to extract, similar to human perception.
evidence: This is a claim about the capabilities of Selfee supported by experimental results.

claim: During the training process, Selfee learns to project images to a low-dimensional space without being affected by shooting conditions, image translation, and rotation, where cosine distance is proper to measure the similarities of original pictures.
source: During the training process, Selfee learns to project images to a low-dimensional space without being affected by shooting conditions, image translation, and rotation, where cosine distance is proper to measure the similarities of original pictures.
evidence: This describes the properties of the learned representations.

claim: Selfee was applied to fruit flies, mice, and rats, three widely used model animals.
source: We apply Selfee to fruit flies, mice, and rats, three widely used model animals, and validate our results with manual annotations or pre-existed animal tracking methods.
evidence: This describes the experimental validation performed in the manuscript.

claim: Discoveries of behavioral phenotypes in mutant flies by Selfee are consistent with either human observations or other animal tracking analysis, and can be validated by biological experiments.
source: Discoveries of behavioral phenotypes in mutant flies by Selfee are consistent with either human observations or other animal tracking analysis, and can be validated by biological experiments.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Grayscale videos are decomposed into single frames, and three tandem frames are stacked into a live-frame to generate a motion-colored RGB picture.
source: First, grayscale videos are decomposed into single frames, and three tandem frames are stacked into a live-frame to generate a motion-colored RGB picture (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the preprocessing step shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Live-frames preserve not only spatial information within each channel but also temporal information across different channels.
source: These live-frames preserve not only spatial information (e.g., postures of each individual or relative distances and angles between individuals) within each channel but also temporal information across different channels.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the properties of live-frames.

claim: Live-frames are used to train Selfee to produce comprehensive and discriminative representations at the frame level.
source: Live-frames are used to train Selfee to produce comprehensive and discriminative representations at the frame level (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the training process shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Anomaly detection on mutant animals can discover new phenotypes compared with their genetic controls.
source: For example, anomaly detection on mutant animals can discover new phenotypes compared with their genetic controls (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: AR-HMM could be applied to model the micro-dynamics of behaviors, such as the duration of states or the probabilities of state transitions.
source: Also, the AR-HMM could be applied to model the micro-dynamics of behaviors, such as the duration of states or the probabilities of state transitions (Wiltschko et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work and demonstrated in the results.

claim: The AR-HMM splits videos into modules and yields behavioral state usages that visualize differences between genotypes.
source: The AR-HMM splits videos into modules and yields behavioral state usages that visualize differences between genotypes (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 1D.

claim: DTW could compare the long-term dynamics of animal behaviors and capture global differences at the video level by aligning pairs of time series and calculating their similarities.
source: In contrast, DTW could compare the long-term dynamics of animal behaviors and capture global differences at the video level (Myers et al., 1980) by aligning pairs of time series and calculating their similarities (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and demonstrated in the results section.

claim: Selfee contains a pair of Siamese CNNs trained to generate discriminative representations for live-frames.
source: Selfee contains a pair of Siamese CNNs trained to generate discriminative representations for live-frames.
evidence: This describes the architecture of Selfee.

claim: ResNet-50 is chosen as the backbone whose classifier layer is replaced by a three-layer multi-layer perceptron (MLP).
source: ResNet-50 (He et al., 2016) is chosen as the backbone whose classifier layer is replaced by a three-layer multi-layer perceptron (MLP).
evidence: This describes the architecture of Selfee with a citation to ResNet-50.

claim: The SimSiam style is the most straightforward Siamese CNN frameworks with only one term of loss.
source: To the best of our knowledge, the SimSiam style is the most straightforward Siamese CNN frameworks with only one term of loss.
evidence: This is a claim about the properties of SimSiam based on the authors' knowledge.

claim: Augmentations applied to live-frames include crop, rotation, flip, and application of the Turbo lookup table followed by color jitters.
source: Augmentations applied to live-frames include crop, rotation, flip, and application of the Turbo lookup table (Mikhailov, 2019) followed by color jitters (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the data augmentation strategy with a citation and figure reference.

claim: To prevent mode collapse, the reference branch will not receive gradient information during optimization.
source: To prevent mode collapse, the reference branch will not receive gradient information during optimization, which means the outcome of the reference branch is detached from the computational graph and treated as ground truth (Figure 2C).
evidence: This describes a training strategy to prevent mode collapse.

claim: On the t-SNE map, human-annotated courtship behaviors were grouped in a non-random pattern.
source: On the t-SNE map, human-annotated courtship behaviors, including chasing, wing extension, copulation attempt, copulation, and non-interactive behaviors ('others'), were grouped in a non-random pattern (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3A and demonstrates that Selfee captures meaningful features.

claim: The features extracted by Selfee separated wing extension behaviors based on the wing angles and male head to female tail distance.
source: We found that the features extracted by Selfee separated wing extension behaviors based on the wing angles (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C) and male head to female tail distance (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is demonstrated in supplementary figures.

claim: The result showed that chasing behavior could be separated based on the positions of male flies in the chamber, which might indicate the thigmotaxis level.
source: The result also showed that chasing behavior could be separated based on the positions of male flies in the chamber, which might indicate the thigmotaxis level.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results with speculation about biological meaning.

claim: Selfee is capable of extracting comprehensive features that consist of human observations or animal tracking results.
source: In conclusion, Selfee is capable of extracting comprehensive features that consist of human observations or animal tracking results, and in this way, Selfee uniforms natural-languages-based human descriptions and engineered features from tracking results in different units (e.g., rad for angle and mm for distance) and scales in a single discriminative Meta-representation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: A weighed k-NN classifier was constructed and achieved a mean F1 score of 72.4% in sevenfold cross-validation on fly courtship behavior classification.
source: Sevenfold cross-validation was performed on the dataset with the k-NN classifier, which achieved a mean F1 score of 72.4% and achieved a similar classification result as human annotations (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the classification experiments.

claim: The classifier had the worst recall score on wing extension behaviors (67% recall), likely because of the ambiguous intermediate states between chasing and wing extension.
source: The classifier had the worst recall score on wing extension behaviors (67% recall, Figure 3B), likely because of the ambiguous intermediate states between chasing and wing extension (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the classification results with supporting figure.

claim: Independent human experts could only reach agreements on around 70% of wing extension frames.
source: It was reported that independent human experts could only reach agreements on around 70% of wing extension frames (Leng et al., 2020), comparable to the performance of our k-NN classifier.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Selfee extracted features achieved comparable results with FlyTracker features or JAABA features, and it achieved the best performance evaluated by Pearson's correlation and F1 score.
source: We found that Selfee extracted features achieved comparable results with FlyTracker features or JAABA features, and it achieved the best performance evaluated by Pearson's correlation and F1 score (Table 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison shown in Table 1.

claim: Additional irrelevant key points marking fly legs would strongly interfere the performance of pure distance-based features.
source: We also found that additional irrelevant key points marking fly legs would strongly interfere the performance of pure distance-based features, indicating that key point choice and feature engineering were crucial for downstream classification.
evidence: This is an observation from the comparison experiments.

claim: Distance-based features were overfocused on subtle differences between frames and neglected differences between major types of behaviors.
source: Results showed that distance-based features were overfocused on subtle differences between frames and neglected differences between major types of behaviors.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the t-SNE visualization results.

claim: Selfee extracted features are as discriminative as classic animal-tracking derived features, but could be used more easily without careful key points definition or dedicated feature engineering.
source: Overall, Selfee extracted features are as discriminative as classic animal-tracking derived features, but could be used more easily without careful key points definition or dedicated feature engineering.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison experiments.

claim: Five types of mice mating behaviors could be separated by Selfee using t-SNE visualization.
source: With t-SNE visualization, we found that five types of behaviors could be separated by Selfee, although mounting behaviors were rare and not concentrated (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Using the LightGBM classifier with temporal features, the average F1 score of eightfold cross-validation could reach 67.4% for mice mating behavior classification.
source: Using the LightGBM (Light Gradient Boosting Machine) classifier (Ke et al., 2017), we achieved a much higher classification performance by incorporating slide moving average and standard deviation of 81-frame time windows, the main frequencies, and their energy within 81-frame time windows. The average F1 score of eightfold cross-validation could reach 67.4%, and the classification results of the ensembled classifier (see Materials and methods) were closed to human observations (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the classification experiments with citation.

claim: Group discriminators were added to vanilla SimSiam networks to fight against the long-tail effect.
source: Therefore, we added group discriminators to vanilla SimSiam networks, which were reported to fight against the long-tail effect proficiently (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes a modification to the architecture with citation.

claim: Group discriminators were helpful for preventing mode collapse during ablation studies.
source: Aside from overcoming the long-tail effect, we also found group discriminators helpful for preventing mode collapse during ablation studies (Figure 3—figure supplement 5B-D and Table 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated in ablation studies shown in supplementary figures and tables.

claim: Applying the Turbo lookup table on grayscale frames brought more complexity and made color distortions more powerful on grayscale images.
source: Aside from CLD loss, Turbo transformation was another customed modification. Applying the Turbo lookup table on grayscale frames brought more complexity and made color distortions more powerful on grayscale images, one of the most critical type of augmentations reported before (Chen et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes a modification with citation to previous work.

claim: Selfee would capture more useful features with Turbo augmentation.
source: Selfee would capture more useful features with this Turbo augmentation (Figure 3—figure supplement 5E, F and Table 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated in ablation studies.

claim: Selfee features extracted from live-frames were more discriminative than those extracted from single frames for mice mating behaviors.
source: Live-frames used by Selfee were also helpful to capture temporal information of animal behaviors, especially for highly dynamic ones such as mice mating behaviors. We found that Selfee features extracted from single frames were less discriminative than those extracted from live-frames (Table 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated in ablation studies shown in Table 3.

claim: The representations produced by Selfee could be directly used for anomaly detection without further post-processing.
source: The representations produced by Selfee could be directly used for anomaly detection without further post-processing.
evidence: This describes a capability of Selfee.

claim: During the training step, Selfee learns to compare Meta-representations of frames with cosine distance which is also used for anomaly detection.
source: During the training step, Selfee learns to compare Meta-representations of frames with cosine distance which is also used for anomaly detection.
evidence: This describes the training objective and its application.

claim: An intra-group score (IAS) is introduced to eliminate false-positive effects in anomaly detection.
source: Therefore, an intra-group score (IAS) is introduced in the second step to eliminate these false-positive effects.
evidence: This describes a methodological improvement for anomaly detection.

claim: CCHa2-R-RB>Kir2.1 flies showed a significantly high anomaly score in male-male interaction videos.
source: The results revealed that one line, CCHa2-R-RB>Kir2.1, showed a significantly high anomaly score.
evidence: This is a result from the genetic screening experiment.

claim: The phenotype of CCHa2-R-RB>Kir2.1 flies was identified as a brief tussle behavior mixed with copulation attempts.
source: By manually going through all anomalous live-frames, we further identified its phenotype as a brief tussle behavior mixed with copulation attempts (Figure 4C, Figure 4—video 1, 0.2× play speed).
evidence: This is a result from manual inspection of anomalous frames.

claim: The tussle behavior of CCHa2-R-RB>Kir2.1 flies was ultra-fast and lasted for less than a quarter second.
source: This behavior was ultra-fast and lasted for less than a quarter second (Figure 4D), making it difficult to be detected by human observers.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Frame-level anomaly detection could capture sub-second behavior episodes that human observers tend to neglect.
source: Up to this point, we have demonstrated that the frame-level anomaly detection could capture sub-second behavior episodes that human observers tend to neglect.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the anomaly detection results.

claim: Trh knock-out flies had close body contact compared to wild-type.
source: Selfee also revealed that Trh (Tryptophan hydroxylase) knock-out flies had close body contact compared to wild-type.
evidence: This is a result from anomaly detection.

claim: Trh is the crucial enzyme for serotonin biosynthesis.
source: Trh is the crucial enzyme for serotonin biosynthesis (Coleman and Neckameyer, 2005), and its mutant flies showed a statistically significantly higher anomaly score (Figure 4B) than the wild-type control.
evidence: This is supported by a citation and experimental results.

claim: Selfee identified 60 frames of abnormal behaviors within 42,000 input frames for Trh mutant flies, occupying less than 0.15% of the total recording time.
source: Selfee identified 60 frames of abnormal behaviors within 42,000 input frames, occupying less than 0.15% of the total recording time.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from anomaly detection.

claim: Serotonin signals were well studied for controlling aggression behavior in flies.
source: Even though serotonin signals were well studied for controlling aggression behavior in flies (Alekseyenko et al., 2014), to the best of our knowledge, the close body contact of flies and serotonergic neurons' role in this behavior has not been reported yet.
evidence: This is supported by a citation and a claim about novelty.

claim: The close body contact of flies and serotonergic neurons' role in this behavior has not been reported yet.
source: Even though serotonin signals were well studied for controlling aggression behavior in flies (Alekseyenko et al., 2014), to the best of our knowledge, the close body contact of flies and serotonergic neurons' role in this behavior has not been reported yet.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding.

claim: Trh knock-out flies had a significantly lower kicking rate than control flies.
source: Our results showed that Trh knock-out flies had a significantly lower kicking rate than control flies (Figure 4G), indicating a reduction of self-defensive intensity.
evidence: This is a result from the defensive behavior assay shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Trh knock-out flies kept significantly shorter distances from others than the control group in social behavior assay.
source: By comparing median values of these distances of each replication, Trh knock-out flies kept significantly shorter distances from others than the control group (Figure 4H, I).
evidence: This is a result from the social behavior assay shown in Figures 4H and 4I.

claim: Trh knock-out flies had reduced self-defensive behavior and social distance.
source: Therefore, we concluded that Trh knock-out flies had reduced self-defensive behavior and social distance, which validated the anomaly detected by Selfee.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple behavioral assays.

claim: Selfee is capable of discovering novel features of animal behaviors with biological relevance when a proper baseline is defined.
source: Taken together, Selfee is capable of discovering novel features of animal behaviors with biological relevance when a proper baseline is defined.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the anomaly detection experiments.

claim: AR-HMM is a powerful method for analyzing stereotyped behavioral data.
source: AR-HMM is a powerful method for analyzing stereotyped behavioral data (Rudolph et al., 2020; Wiltschko et al., 2015; Wiltschko et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: AR-HMM discovers modules of behaviors and describes the modules with autoregressive matrixes.
source: It discovers modules of behaviors and describes the modules with autoregressive matrixes.
evidence: This describes the functionality of AR-HMM.

claim: PCA of state usages revealed an apparent difference between mice with and without CIS experience.
source: PCA of state usages revealed an apparent difference between mice with and without CIS experience (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Usages of two modules (No.0 and No.3) showed statistically significant differences between the control and CIS groups.
source: Usages of two modules (No.0 and No.3) showed statistically significant differences between the two groups (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C with statistical analysis.

claim: Mice in the CIS group spent more time near walls while mice in the control group spent more time in the central area.
source: Mice in the CIS group spent more time near walls while mice in the control group spent more time in the central area (Figure 5C, blue and red lines), and similar observations had been reported before (Ramirez et al., 2015).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C and supported by a citation.

claim: Mice performing behavior No.0 were relatively distant from walls, while in module No. 3, mice were closer to the border.
source: The result indicated that mice performing behavior No.0 were relatively distant from walls, while in module No. 3, mice were closer to the border (Figure 5C, cyan and yellow bars).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Selfee with AR-HMM successfully distinguished mice in the control group from the CIS group, and the differences spotted by Selfee were consistent with previous observations.
source: These results showed that Selfee with AR-HMM successfully distinguished mice in the control group from the CIS group, and the differences spotted by Selfee were consistent with previous observations (Ramirez et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the AR-HMM analysis with citation.

claim: DTW is a well-known algorithm for aligning time series, which returns the best-matched path and the matching similarity.
source: DTW is a well-known algorithm for aligning time series, which returns the best-matched path and the matching similarity (Figure 5E).
evidence: This describes the functionality of DTW with figure reference.

claim: NorpA mutant flies have defective visual transduction.
source: Visual cues are essential for male flies to locate female flies during courtship (Ribeiro et al., 2018), and mutant flies of NorpA, which have defective visual transduction (Bloomquist et al., 1988), have a prolonged courtship latency in our experiments (Figure 5F), similar to previously findings (Markow and Manning, 1980).
evidence: This is supported by citations and experimental results shown in Figure 5F.

claim: NorpA mutant flies have a prolonged courtship latency.
source: Visual cues are essential for male flies to locate female flies during courtship (Ribeiro et al., 2018), and mutant flies of NorpA, which have defective visual transduction (Bloomquist et al., 1988), have a prolonged courtship latency in our experiments (Figure 5F), similar to previously findings (Markow and Manning, 1980).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5F and supported by citations.

claim: When wild-type flies were used as the reference for the DTW, the group of NorpA mutant flies yielded a curve lower than the diagonal line, indicating a delay in their courtship behaviors.
source: When wild-type flies were used as the reference for the DTW, the group of NorpA mutant flies yielded a curve lower than the diagonal line, indicating a delay in their courtship behaviors (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Selfee and DTW could capture differences in long-term dynamics such as behavior latency.
source: In this way, our experiments confirm that Selfee and DTW could capture differences in long-term dynamics such as behavior latency.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the DTW analysis.

claim: DTW and AR-HMM could capture temporal differences between control and experimental groups beyond single-frame postures.
source: In conclusion, DTW and AR-HMM could capture temporal differences between control and experimental groups beyond single-frame postures, making Selfee a competent unsupervised method for traditional analyses like courtship index or copulation latency.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temporal analysis results.

claim: Only 12 frames of anomaly behaviors were sorted out in the CIS group, contributing to less than 0.01% of all frames.
source: In the CIS group, 12 frames of anomaly behaviors were sorted out (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A). However, these anomaly frames with their score slightly higher than the threshold only contributed to less than 0.01% of all frames, and occurred only in 2 out of 17 videos.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from anomaly detection.

claim: The 12 anomalous frames in the CIS group were classified as false-positive after being examined manually.
source: Therefore, these frames were classified as false-positive after being examined manually (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a result from manual inspection.

claim: AR-HMM separated the control and CIS groups apart, and the major differences were related to mice's distances to the arena walls.
source: As previously showed, AR-HMM separated two groups apart, and the major differences were related to mice's distances to the arena walls (Figure 5D).
evidence: This refers back to previous results shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Results generated from Selfee embeddings were strongly consistent with those from mice positions in DTW analysis.
source: When delays of the control group were isolated, we found results generated from Selfee embeddings were strongly consistent with those from mice positions (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The pipeline with Selfee and downstream analysis could evaluate animal behaviors in a purely unsupervised way.
source: In conclusion, our pipeline with Selfee and downstream analysis could evaluate animal behaviors in a purely unsupervised way.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the capabilities of the method.

claim: The method requires no human definition of either animal behaviors, or key points of animal skeletons, and thus subjective factors that would bias the analysis are avoided.
source: The method requires no human definition of either animal behaviors, or key points of animal skeletons, and thus subjective factors that would bias the analysis are avoided.
evidence: This is a claim about the advantages of the unsupervised approach.

claim: Siamese CNNs have proven their capability to learn comprehensive representations.
source: Siamese CNNs have proven their capability to learn comprehensive representations (Chen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: The cosine similarity, part of the loss function used for training, is rational and well suited to measure similarities between the raw images.
source: The cosine similarity, part of its loss function used for training, is rational and well suited to measure similarities between the raw images.
evidence: This is a claim about the properties of the training objective.

claim: CNNs are trained end-to-end so that preprocessing steps like segmentation or key points extraction is unnecessary.
source: Besides, CNNs are trained end-to-end so that preprocessing steps like segmentation or key points extraction is unnecessary.
evidence: This is a claim about the advantages of end-to-end training.

claim: The extracted representations could be used not only for straightforward distance-based analyses such as t-SNE visualization or k-NN anomaly detection but also for sophisticated post-processing methods like AR-HMM.
source: By incorporating Selfee with different post-processing methods, we can identify phenotypes of animal behaviors at different time scales. In the current work, we demonstrate that the extracted representations could be used not only for straightforward distance-based analyses such as t-SNE visualization or k-NN anomaly detection but also for sophisticated post-processing methods like AR-HMM.
evidence: This is demonstrated through various analyses in the results section.

claim: Selfee features could be used flexibly with different machine learning methods for various experimental purposes.
source: Therefore, Selfee features could be used flexibly with different machine learning methods for various experimental purposes.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the versatility of Selfee features.

claim: Selfee could serve as a helpful complement of the widely used pose estimation methods in multi-animal behavior analysis, and vice versa.
source: By applying our method to mice mating behavior and fly courtship behaviors, we show that Selfee could serve as a helpful complement of the widely used pose estimation methods in multi-animal behavior analysis, and vice versa.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison with pose estimation methods.

claim: Selfee features are proved to be comparably discriminative as key points derived human-engineered features.
source: First, Selfee features are proved to be comparably discriminative as key points derived human-engineered features.
evidence: This is supported by the comparison experiments in Table 1.

claim: The current version of DeepLabCut could hardly extract useful features during intromission behaviors of two black mice.
source: We found that the current version of DeepLabCut could hardly extract useful features during intromission behaviors of two black mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is shown in supplementary figures and videos.

claim: It was extremely difficult to unambiguously label body parts like nose, ears and hips when two mice were close enough, a task challenging even for human experts.
source: The reason was that it was extremely difficult to unambiguously label body parts like nose, ears and hips when two mice were close enough, a task challenging even for human experts.
evidence: This is an explanation for the difficulty of pose estimation.

claim: Inaccurate tracking of fly wings and fly bodies was observed in FlyTracker results.
source: We visualized tracking results provided by the Fly-vs-Fly dataset (Fleet et al., 2014), which used classic computer vision techniques for tracking, and inaccurate tracking of fly wings and fly bodies was observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B, Figure 1—video 2).
evidence: This is shown in supplementary figures and videos.

claim: The same type of error occurred when flies showed intensive body contact in SLEAP tracking results.
source: To investigate if cutting-edge deep learning methods would avoid such problems, we labeled 3000 frames to train a SLEAP (Pereira et al., 2022) model and inferred on a clip of a fly courtship video. Unfortunately, the same type of error occurred when flies showed intensive body contact (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C, Figure 1—video 3).
evidence: This is shown in supplementary figures and videos.

claim: Key point detection for closely interacting or overlapped animals is still challenging.
source: By testing these three representative pose estimation programs, we argue that key point detection for closely interacting or overlapped animals is still challenging.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from testing multiple pose estimation methods.

claim: Selfee methods could capture global characteristics of behaviors like human perception, making it robust to confusing occlusions.
source: By contrast, our methods could capture global characteristics of behaviors like human perception, making it robust to these confusing occlusions.
evidence: This is a claim about the advantages of Selfee over pose estimation.

claim: Selfee features appear less explainable than key points.
source: Nevertheless, Selfee features appear less explainable than key points, and we have shown that animal tracking was very useful for interpreting Selfee features.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation of Selfee.

claim: Selfee strongly complements the incapability of pose estimation methods processing closely contacted animals.
source: Therefore, Selfee strongly complements the incapability of pose estimation methods processing closely contacted animals, and could be further improved to be more explainable when assisted by animal tracking.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the complementary nature of Selfee and pose estimation.

claim: Modern self-supervised learning neural networks usually require at least eight modern GPUs even TPUs for training.
source: Modern self-supervised learning neural networks usually require at least eight modern GPUs (Caron et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2021) even TPUs (Chen et al., 2020; Grill et al., 2020) for training, take advantage of batch sizes larger than 1024, and training time varies from several days to a week.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Selfee model can be trained on only one RTX 3090 GPU with a batch size of 256 within only 8 hr.
source: In contrast, our model can be trained on only one RTX 3090 GPU with a batch size of 256 within only 8 hr with the help of the newly proposed CLD loss function (Wang et al., 2021) and other improvements (see Materials and methods for further details).
evidence: This is a quantitative claim about the training efficiency with citation.

claim: Selfee model could achieve zero-shot domain transfer.
source: Nevertheless, we found that our model could achieve zero-shot domain transfer.
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments on OFT and rat behaviors.

claim: Selfee trained for mating behavior of a pair of mice could also be applied to OFTs of single animal.
source: We demonstrated that Selfee trained for mating behavior of a pair of mice could also be applied to OFTs of single animal.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the results section.

claim: Assisted by AR-HMM, Selfee captured the major differences between mice in the control and CIS groups.
source: Assisted by AR-HMM, Selfee captured the major differences between mice in the control and CIS groups.
evidence: This is demonstrated in the results section.

claim: When the model pre-trained with mice videos was applied to rat behaviors, a zero-shot classification of five major types of social behaviors was achieved with an F1 score of 49.6%.
source: Furthermore, when the model pre-trained with mice videos was applied to rat behaviors, we were able to achieve a zero-shot classification of five major types of social behaviors (Figure 3—figure supplement 4). Although the F1 score was only 49.6%, it still captured the major differences between similar behaviors, such as allogrooming and social nose contact (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Self-supervised learning could be easily achieved with limited computation resources and a much shorter time and could be directly transferred to datasets that share similar visual characteristics.
source: Thus, we have demonstrated that self-supervised learning could be easily achieved with limited computation resources and a much shorter time and could be directly transferred to datasets that share similar visual characteristics and save more resources.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the training efficiency and zero-shot transfer results.

claim: Each live-frame only contains three raw frames, so the model could not capture much information on the animal motion.
source: First, because each live-frame only contains three raw frames, our model could not capture much information on the animal motion.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation.

claim: CNNs are highly vulnerable to image texture.
source: Second, as previously reported, CNNs are highly vulnerable to image texture (Geirhos et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Certain types of beddings of the behavior chamber could profoundly affect the performance of Selfee neural networks.
source: We observed that certain types of beddings of the behavior chamber could profoundly affect the performance of our neural networks (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), so in some cases, background removal is necessary (see Materials and methods for further details).
evidence: This is shown in supplementary figures.

claim: Selfee could only use discriminative features within each batch, without any negative samples provided, so minor irrelevant differences could be amplified and cause inconsistent results (mode-split).
source: Lastly, Selfee could only use discriminative features within each batch, without any negative samples provided, so minor irrelevant differences could be amplified and cause inconsistent results (named mode-split).
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation.

claim: Advanced self-supervised learning methods like DINO (with visual transformers, ViTs) could separate objects from the background and extract more explainable representations.
source: On the one hand, advanced self-supervised learning methods like DINO (Caron et al., 2021) (with visual transformers, ViTs) could separate objects from the background and extract more explainable representations.
evidence: This is supported by a citation and discusses future directions.

claim: Using ViTs, the neural network could be more robust against distractive textures.
source: Besides, by using ViTs, the neural network could be more robust against distractive textures (Naseer et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and discusses future directions.

claim: Training Selfee only takes 8 hr on a single RTX 3090 GPU, and the inference speed could reach 800 frames per second.
source: Training Selfee only takes 8 hr on a single RTX 3090 GPU (graphic card), and the inference speed could reach 800 frames per second.
evidence: This is a quantitative claim about computational efficiency.

claim: Selfee could accept top-view 2D grayscale video frames as inputs so that neither depth cameras nor fine-calibrated multi-view camera arrays are required.
source: Selfee could accept top-view 2D grayscale video frames as inputs so that neither depth cameras (Wiltschko et al., 2015) nor fine-calibrated multi-view camera arrays (Huang et al., 2021) are required.
evidence: This describes the input requirements with citations.

claim: Selfee can be trained and used with routinely collected behavior videos on ordinary desktop workstations, warranting its accessibility to biology laboratories.
source: Therefore, Selfee can be trained and used with routinely collected behavior videos on ordinary desktop workstations, warranting its accessibility to biology laboratories.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the accessibility of the method.
